Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Mist WebSocket transport and eager runtime initialization

Introduce direct Sky-to-Cocoon WebSocket transport (B7-S6) eliminating the Mountain gRPC hop for ~95% of extension-API IPC volume. The new MistWebSocketTransport handles authentication via subprotocol/query param, exponential backoff reconnection (100ms-5s, dead after 30s), and request/response correlation.

Key changes:
- LandWorkbenchRuntime: Switch from lazy to eager ManagedRuntime initialization via IIFE at module load, removing first-call latency and ensuring single runtime instance across Sky chunks.
- FileSystemProviderImplementation: Replace Effect.runPromise(IPCService.invoke) with direct @tauri-apps/api/core invoke for MountainIPCInvoke.
- MistWebSocketTransport (new): Full WebSocket client with pending request map, health checks, and notify/invoke APIs.
- TauriMainProcessService: Add WebSocket routing tier checked before Node tier; InitializeWebSocket() entry point for Sky bootstrap.

Impact: Reduced IPC latency for extension host communication, simpler Tauri invoke path, and foundation for Mountain gRPC offload.

Message:
feat(Wind): Add per-subsystem IPC routing tiers to Tier utility

Introduce 14 new type definitions and their corresponding Tier object entries in `Source/Utility/Tier.ts` for per-subsystem routing, mirroring Cocoon's routing tiers: Terminal, SCM, Debug, LanguageFeatures, Search, OutputChannel, NativeHost, TreeView, Storage, Model, Tasks, Auth, Encryption, ExtensionHost, and WebSocket.

Each subsystem gets its own union type (e.g. TierTerminalValue = "Mountain" | "Node") and a Tier entry with a static default that matches the values in `.env.Land` and `Mountain/build.rs::EmitTierDefaults`. The ExtensionHost and WebSocket tiers use distinct value sets (Process/WebWorker/Disabled and Disabled/Mountain/Mist respectively) reflecting their unique routing semantics.

This enables the Wind service layer to resolve per-subsystem IPC routing at runtime rather than relying on a single global IPC tier, laying the groundwork for fine-grained traffic splitting between Mountain native backend and Cocoon Node host.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:

Extended the IPC subsystem to support a new `NodeDeferred` routing tier, enabling seamless fallback to the Cocoon Node.js runtime when Mountain/Tauri handlers are unavailable. This introduces a three-tier configuration via the `TierIPC` environment variable:
- `Mountain` (default): Direct invocation via Tauri.
- `NodeDeferred`: Attempt Tauri first; on failure, forward requests to the Cocoon Node.js extension host via the `cocoon:request` bridge.
- `Node`: Route all traffic directly to Cocoon, bypassing the Tauri layer.

Implemented the `_InvokeViaNode` helper to facilitate relay calls through Mountain's gRPC bridge, ensuring compatibility with `__TAURI__` and `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` globals.

Message:

The `ResolveConfiguration` function previously assumed the Tauri IPC globals (`__TAURI_INTERNALS__` or `__TAURI__`) were immediately available. In certain webview load orderings or with the specific Mountain fork, these globals may be undefined during initial module evaluation, causing the configuration fetch to fail prematurely.

Introduce a 5-second polling loop with a 25ms interval that retries detection of the `Invoke` function. If the IPC bridge remains unavailable after the deadline, log a diagnostic message via `DevLog` and proceed with default path fallbacks. This ensures the workbench can boot in degraded mode rather than stalling indefinitely during initialization, while still attempting to recover native functionality if the bridge becomes ready shortly after start.

The update refactors the IPC resolution logic into a reusable `ResolveInvoke` helper and wraps the invocation with explicit TypeScript casting to satisfy the type checker.

- Successful "tauri-invoke" completions logged every invoke (redundant - Mountain's Rust side already logs ok/fail with ns precision via `[DEV:IPC] done:`)
- All fire-and-forget channel stubs logged (noop/value cases are routine)

This caused keystroke lag as user input queued behind the log noise on the shared WebKit message channel. Fix removes:
- Success-case tauri-invoke forward (failures still forwarded - stack traces are worth the cost)
- Fire-and-forget channel stub logging entirely
- Only forward `drift` disposition case (the noteworthy scenario)

Catalog version bumped to 2026-05-01 reflecting codegen run.

Message:

Add no-op stubs for two high-frequency IPC channels that were causing
unnecessary Tauri round-trips:

- `telemetryAppender`: VS Code's TelemetryChannelAppender posts every
event through the shared-process channel. Land has no shared process or
telemetry backend, so each call fell through to
`InvokeMountain("undefined:log")`. Observed at 155 calls per boot in

- `mcpGalleryManifest`: MCP extension marketplace manifest bootstrap.
`channel-stub` surfaced this as the sole remaining `miss` per session.
The workbench calls `setMcpGalleryManifest({...})` once at boot; a no-op
stub is sufficient until Land has an MCP registry.

Also enhance `_DevLogForward` to send both casings (Tag/Message AND
tag/message) so Tauri's param-case handling doesn't require a guess -
the Rust command coalesces whichever arrived populated. Add fallback to
`__TAURI_INTERNALS__` for broader Tauri version compatibility.

Impact: Eliminates ~156 unnecessary Tauri IPC round-trips per editor
boot, reducing startup latency.

- Misses (when neither route nor stub exists)

Add a native-host dialog bridge to IPCRendererShim that intercepts Electron-style dialog IPC channels (`nativeHost:showOpenDialog`, `vscode:showOpenDialog`, etc.) and translates them to Tauri's dialog API.

- Add TelemetryLive layer to Bootstrap configuration

All polyfills now check for Tauri 2.x first (core.invoke), then fall back to 1.x patterns, ensuring backward compatibility with existing Tauri 1.x deployments while enabling Tauri 2.x upgrades.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Tauri-native IPC routing and complete workbench configuration

Implement two parallel IPC pathways to replace Electron's ipcMain:

1. **IPCRendererShim binary protocol loopback**: Re-implement VS Code's binary IPC serialization (SerializeIPC/DeserializeIPC) to handle vscode:message events with loopback responses. Provides stub handlers for channels (logger, storage, configuration, localFilesystem) to prevent workbench hangs.

2. **TauriMainProcessService**: New drop-in replacement for ElectronIPCMainProcessService that routes channel.call() directly through Tauri invoke to Mountain's WindServiceHandlers. Eliminates binary protocol overhead entirely - uses plain JSON over Tauri commands.

3. **ResolveConfiguration**: Extend with full INativeWindowConfiguration including profiles, colorScheme, accessibilitySupport, and other DesktopMain fields. Also fix appRoot to strip origin (workbench prepends vscode-file://), and set VSCODE_DEV: "true" for relative imports.

This enables the VS Code workbench to initialize in the Tauri webview with either protocol path.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Wind): Enable WKWebView compatibility with relative imports

Set VSCODE_DEV: "true" in both Install.ts userEnv and ProcessPolyfill default config. This tells the Electron workbench to use relative imports instead of vscode-file:// URLs, resolving the WKWebView (macOS) limitation where custom URL schemes cannot be used with import().

Also fix potential null reference in ProcessPolyfill by deferring hrtimeStart initialization. The previous code called process.hrtime() at module evaluation time, but Wind sets window.vscode.process after Install.ts runs, not globalThis.process. Initialize to [0, 0] and let the actual timer start lazily.

These changes enable the VS Code workbench to render properly in the Tauri webview on macOS.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add History, Label, Model, and TextModelResolver services

Implement four new Effect-TS service layers in Wind that connect to Mountain via Tauri IPC:

- **HistoryService**: Manages editor navigation stack for back/forward traversal. IPC: history:goBack, goForward, canGoBack, canGoForward, push, clear, getStack.

- **LabelService**: Resolves human-readable display labels for URIs, workspace roots, and filenames (used in explorer, tabs, breadcrumbs). IPC: label:getUri, getWorkspace, getBase.

- **ModelService**: Lightweight in-memory text model registry. Maintains open documents with content/version/languageId. IPC: model:open, close, get, getAll, updateContent.

- **TextModelResolverService**: Resolves URIs to text model references with reference-counting dispose pattern (VS Code IReference<ITextModel>). Delegates to ModelService with ref counting.

Each service includes interface, stub implementation, live IPC layer, mock layer, Effect Context tag, and problem types following Wind's established pattern.

Also refactor TauriIPC invoke to use unified "mountain_ipc_invoke" command with {method, params} structure, and update all layer composition files to use Layer.provideMerge() chaining.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
chore(Wind): Add .gitignore for build artifacts and IDE files

This commit adds a new .gitignore file to the Wind Element to prevent ephemeral build artifacts and development configuration from being committed to the repository.

Changes include:
- Target build outputs (excluding debug/release folders)
- Configuration bundles (TypeScript/ESBuild outputs)
- Node.js dependencies (.node_modules)
- Environment files (.env, .env.local)
- Log files (*.log)
- IDE configuration (.vscode/, .idea/)

This aligns with standard project hygiene practices, ensuring that build artifacts and local developer settings are excluded while maintaining the necessary folder structure in the repository.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
build(Wind): Regenerate development build artifacts with source maps

This commit reverses the production build from the previous commit, regenerating the Wind Element's build artifacts in development mode. The key changes:

- **Configuration/ESBuild**: All configuration files in `Configuration/ESBuild/` and `Target/Configuration/ESBuild/` have been regenerated from minified to readable format with proper variable names and formatting.
- **Source Maps**: Added `.js.map` files for all Configuration/ESBuild modules to enable debugging.
- **Target Artifacts**: Regenerated all target build outputs in `Target/` directory with full source maps.
- **Documentation**: Added comprehensive 50-level analysis documentation block to `Source/Preload.ts`.

This aligns with the development workflow, switching from the production build (commit 40c5ac0) to enable debugging and development. The build now includes readable code and source maps for both the Configuration bundles and Target application artifacts.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
build(Wind): Generate production build artifacts (minified + no source maps)

This commit runs the production build process for the Wind Element, updating the build outputs in both `Target` and `Configuration` directories.

Key changes:
- **Minification**: All JavaScript files in `Target` (application logic) and `Configuration` (build config bundles) have been minified, reducing file sizes significantly.
- **Source Map Removal**: All `.js.map` files have been deleted to strip debugging information for the production release.
- **Tree Shaking**: Unused type definitions in `Target/Bootstrap/Types` have been removed or emptied.
- **Type Updates**: TypeScript declaration maps (`.d.ts.map`) in `Target/Source` have been regenerated.

This aligns with the release/production workflow, optimizing the bundle size and removing debug artifacts.
